definition: The coordinating service at the center of the book's design: it keeps durable records and checks each change it governs before that change takes effect.
The person who runs a machine and answers for the workers on it.
A program, usually built around a language model, that observes its task and proposes actions such as edits, test runs or payments.
The governed environment agents work in, run by a daemon that holds the shared record and decides, for each change an agent proposes, whether that change takes effect.
A background service; in this book, the trusted program that holds a harbor's shared record and makes the admission check.
The single check in the write path that decides whether a proposed change takes effect; to admit a change is to let it pass this check and go ahead, and the book uses the word in no other sense.
The daemon's authoritative account of who holds which resources, who owes what and what has been paid.
A recorded permission stating what its holder may do, to which resources and until when.
A grant signed by the daemon, which the daemon checks before it admits a change the holder proposes.
A private working copy of a repository, separate from the owner's copy and from other teams' copies.
A description of a change that has not yet happened, such as a patch an agent offers.
A change that has actually happened to a file, a record, a payment or another resource.
The case file for a job: who requested it, what actions are allowed, what has been observed and what remains to be done.
A recorded requirement, such as supplying a test result before a job may be called complete.
The component that actually changes a resource, for example by writing a file.
A grant that one worker holds alone until it expires or is handed on.
The program around a language model that runs it, calls tools for it and returns what the tools observed.
A property the shared state must satisfy before and after every admitted change, such as at most one current holder of a lease.
The kind of source an observation comes from (a check, a signature, a meter, a judgment, a choice or a later outcome), each with its own blind spot.
A test, type checker or model checker, which shows exactly the property it checks under its stated assumptions and nothing more.

A signature, hash, inclusion proof or append-only log that shows which key signed a record, or that a log committed to it, and whether it was altered since, but not that the record is true or complete.
A counter that the party being measured cannot rewrite; it shows a quantity, not its cause.
An assessment under a named rubric, which carries the assessor's error rate.
Evidence of what a buyer chose, which does not show that the choice was right.
Evidence of what eventually happened, which arrives too late to prevent it.
A plan an agent has committed to, which steers what it does next and persists while it tries alternatives.
The belief-desire-intention model of an agent, which represents what it believes, what it wants and what it has committed to do.
In a model of belief or knowledge, one way circumstances could be; an agent believes a statement when it holds in every world the agent regards as possible.
A rule stating when an agent may reconsider an intention.
A temporal operator under which a condition may hold forever if the event that would end it never occurs.
In AgentSpeak, the store of propositions an agent currently believes.
In AgentSpeak, the collection of procedures, each with a trigger and a context, that an agent can adopt.
In AgentSpeak, the record of the remaining steps of a plan the agent has adopted.
A rule saying what an agent must, must not or may do, often with a deadline and a sanction for violation.
A store of general norms from which specific norm instances are created.
A store of the specific norm instances currently in force for particular agents and situations.
A rule for conflicting norms that chooses the feasible set of norms to satisfy so that the largest sanction left unmet is as small as possible.
A queue that holds messages for a receiver until it is ready to process them.
A communication in which the sender waits until the receiver takes the message, so both act at the same moment.
A unit of computation with private state that receives and sends messages, creates other actors and chooses its next behavior.
Making the resource itself refuse a former lease holder once the lease has been given to a successor.
A periodic message by which a worker shows it is still running; a missed one may mean delay rather than failure.
The study of what a speaker does in saying something, separating the words, the act performed (a request, a promise) and its consequences.
A record of an operation, such as a test run, naming what was done and on which revision.
Smith's 1980 protocol in which a manager announces a task, contractors bid and the manager awards the work.
In dynamic epistemic logic, a description of an observation as a set of events, each with a precondition, together with the events each agent cannot tell apart.
Keeping a worker from passing information out except through permitted channels.
An isolated environment that limits which files, network destinations and processes a program can reach.
The property that secret inputs make no difference to what an observer can see.
A group of agents working on related tasks.
A rule that turns every voter's ranking of the alternatives into one collective ranking.
One of the word pieces a language model reads and writes.
The stored keys and values a language model has already computed for earlier positions, reused so that each new token need not recompute them.
The ratio of arithmetic operations to bytes moved to and from memory, which decides whether a computation is limited by compute or by memory bandwidth.
The text a language model can see at once.
Describes an operation that has the same effect however many times it is repeated, so retrying it is safe.
A model of deciding under uncertainty in which the agent cannot see the state directly and must act on a probability distribution over states.
A packaged procedure for one kind of task; in a coding harness, a set of instructions and scripts loaded when needed.
A model that scores each intermediate step of a reasoning chain, not only the final answer.
Keeping only an index of skills in the context window and loading a skill's detailed instructions when it is needed.
In supervisory control, a controller that watches a system's events and can disable the controllable ones.
A script a harness runs at a fixed point, such as just before a tool call, which can refuse the call or record what happened.
The property that every route to an effect passes through the check.
Text written so that a language model reading it will follow it as an instruction; where the model is asked to judge that text, it changes the judgment without changing the model.
Coordination through marks left in a shared environment, which later workers read instead of receiving direct messages.
A record announcing that a worker intends to work on something; it prevents collisions only if conflicting writes must pass a check that consults it.
A number attached to a lease that rises each time the lease changes hands, so the resource can refuse writes from an earlier holder.
The narrowing of a grant at each hand-off: a delegated grant never covers more, or lasts longer, than the grant it came from.
The person or organization on whose behalf an agent acts and who answers for it.
